answer_raw: {"decision":"REJECT","reason":"The patch introduces a scoped regression in the very test file it modifies. In the post-patch run of sympy/printing/tests/test_repr.py, test_set FAILS: `assert srepr(s) == \"set()\"` yields '{}' instead of 'set()'. The new `_print_set` unconditionally emits '{%s}', so the empty set prints as '{}' (which is actually an empty dict literal) rather than the required 'set()'. This failure is absent from the pre-patch baseline (where test_set did not exist and the run showed only the two pre-existing parse_expr failures test_Add/test_Mul), so it is a regression introduced by this patch, not a pre-existing environment failure. The artifact is linked (patch_sha256 and base_commit match), fresh (run tree matches the authoritative restaged tree), and coverage-complete (1/1 F2P, 40/40 P2P executed), so the failure is applicable and decisive. Note also that the maintainer summary's claim of 40/40 P2P passing is contradicted by the actual run log, which shows test_set FAILED.","evidence_mismatch":false,"missing_evidence":"","evidence_gap":"contradiction"}
